q: Shannon entropy H(X) = -∑p(x)log p(x) achieves its maximum for a discrete random variable with n outcomes when:
opts: p is concentrated at one point (deterministic)
p is the uniform distribution (p(x)=1/n for all x)
p has exactly two non-zero values
exp: Shannon entropy is maximised by the uniform distribution: H(X)≤log n with equality iff X is uniform. Intuitively, maximum uncertainty equals maximum information content — a uniform source is maximally hard to compress.
